title: Modify curve end
tagline: Move one end of a curve, chain or wire to a new point and blend the change back -- hold part of the curve exactly, keep G1/G2 there, and match the end to a reference.

slides.title: What it does
slides.problem: Moving an end of a network curve usually means redrawing it. Modify curve end edits the curve's own control points: the end goes where you ask, the change fades back, and whatever you hold stays exactly as it was.
useWhen: Stretch a curve to a new corner of the network
Keep most of a curve untouched
Land an end tangent (or curvature-continuous) to an edge, face or mate connector
slides.caption: T01 move, T30 hold, T10 match an arc (G2).

points.head: Control points, not a refit
points.body: Free control points move by a share of the offset that fades by arc length; the last moves fully.

points.head: Exact hold
points.body: Knots at the hold make the held part depend only on locked control points; G1 / G2 lock one / two more.

points.head: Closed-form end
points.body: Tangent (and curvature) of an edge, face or mate connector set directly on the last control points.

slides.title: The dialog
params: An edge, a chain in any order, or a wire; open, unbranched.
The end to move (empty = the chain's end).
Where it goes (empty = stays / snaps onto the reference).
Hold by Point or Distance (arc length from the modified end).
Transition type; continuity at the fixed end / hold (G0 / G1 / G2); end reference.
+ face: only the part after the hold is projected (G1 kept at the hold).
Degree, tolerance, max control points of a merged chain, sampling multiple, print.

slides.title: End reference (in Parameters)
params: An edge, a face or a mate connector.
G0 / G1 / G2 at the moved end.
100 mm; bends toward the connector's X, else the edge's normal, else the curve's own.
No effect any more (kept for saved features).

slides.title: Example: hold point (T30)
slides.head: End (200, 0) -> (200, 30); hold at (150, -30), G1
slides.body: Everything from the fixed end to the hold is unchanged (under 1 micron); the tangent at the hold is kept. T10: matching an R25 arc gives end curvature 40/m, as the arc.

keys: The end at the To point.
The hold point, or the fixed end when there is no hold.
messages: Notes: no Modified end picked, hold has no effect, G0 hold leaves a corner, reference far away, handle shortened, projection keeps G1 only
hold point missing or at the modified end; hold distance longer than the curve

items.head: Hold instead of G2 everywhere
items.body: A hold keeps the part you care about exactly; blend only the rest.

items.head: Mate connector reference
items.body: Z = the end tangent, X = the bend side; set a radius for exact end curvature (T13).

items.head: Projection
items.body: Keeps the end tangent only if it lies in the face; end curvature cannot be kept.
